text:
ivy: heads up - ran into a browser-specific chunk reassembly issue in the js-sample when combined with our auth refresh. Chrome sometimes emits two small chunks as separate data events and our SSE parser treats the second as a stray fragment, dropping the trailing json.

sam: can you show minimal repro? is this only in browser or also node?

ijordan: fwiw node fetch + our node sdk handled the same stream fine. this looks like how EventSource / ReadableStream chunk boundaries are exposed in the browser.

ivy: repro steps: start a 45s stream, set token to expire mid-stream, force refresh via sample's auto-refresh, then rapidly abort+reconnect sequence in the client. sometimes final object is malformed: missing closing brace. stack: Chrome 114, ios safari also shows different behavior.

ivy: client console excerpt:
```
SSE: data chunk 1: '{"choices":[{"delta":"hel'
SSE: data chunk 2: 'lo","index":0}]}'
SSE parser: emit object failed: unexpected end of input
```

leo: that indicates parsing expects each SSE 'data:' line to be a full JSON blob. But our generator intentionally breaks tokens to keep chunks small. The SDK should buffer across data events until a newline-delimited event is complete.

sam: do we do that in the js sdk? I thought we had a streaming parser that concatenates until '\n\n' boundary.

ivy: yes, but the race is the auth refresh -> fetch abort sequence. When the fetch aborts, some browsers will fire a 'close' before the second data event arrives, so our parser gets a partial buffer and throws rather than preserving partials for resume. node and python can sometimes read the remainder because they keep the socket open longer.

jordan: two quick fixes: 1) parser-level: don't raise on partial JSON when stream is still open; instead stash partial buffer and only error if stream closes and buffer is non-empty (then convert to a well-formed error including last sequence id). 2) SDK-level: on auth-refresh abort, attempt a small micro-wait (50ms) before tearing down the fetch to allow final micro-chunks to arrive; add as opt-in behavior in js-sample.

leo: for long-term, we should improve resume semantics so resume token encodes byte offset + seq id; server could send a compact finalization marker that is sent atomically (e.g., final chunk flagged and retried). But that requires runtime + server changes.

sam: agree. short-term: ivy, can you open PR to update js parser to buffer partial JSONs (no immediate throw) and add test for aborted mid-event? add a comment in sample app with opt-in micro-wait and a flag for 'graceOnAuthRefreshMs'.

ivy: yes. i'll add two unit tests: browser-like chunk boundary and abort-mid-event. will add cross-browser note in README.

ci-bot: created task DEVEX-2248 and started ci job for js-sample parser tests.

jordan: also add an integration test in sdk-parity that runs the curl repro with varied inter-chunk delays and verifies the client receives a complete JSON sequence. That will catch regressions across sdk implementations.

sam: last ask: let's standardize our SSE generator to never split inside a UTF-8 codepoint or inside a JSON token if possible; might reduce probability of harmful splits. runtime team: can we add a 'prefer-safe-splits' flag?

leo: I'll file a runtime RFC for 'split-safety' heuristics and final-chunk re-send policy. POC will target not splitting between ASCII punctuation and within multibyte sequences.

ivy: thanks. i'll push the parser fix and the sample opt-in grace flag today, link to DEVEX-2248.

sam: awesome. please cc sdk owners so they can pick up same pattern for other langs.

ivy: noted, will ping them after PR. thanks!
